is_anopheles.evidence: Mosquitoes collected were morphologically and molecularly confirmed as Anopheles funestus (Page 2, 'Mosquito collection and molecular identification').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study performed species identification PCR and biochemical enzyme assays (P450, GST, esterases), but did not report genotyping of any target resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts, allele counts, or genotype frequencies are reported for any target marker.

african_field_population.evidence: Blood-fed An. funestus females were collected in October 2014 from living rooms in Gbanikola District, Bangui, Central African Republic (Page 2, 'Mosquito collection and molecular identification').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting bioassay and biochemical assay results from field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data are reported for Gbanikola District, Bangui (N 04°20.436'; E 018°32.213') (Page 2, 'Study area').

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collections were conducted in October 2014 (Page 2, 'Mosquito collection and molecular identification').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary study with field sampling conducted specifically for this investigation in Bangui, CAR.

supplement.evidence: No external supplementary files are needed as no target marker genotyping was performed.

assessment.summary: This study reports insecticide susceptibility bioassays (WHO tube assays with permethrin, deltamethrin, lambda-cyhalothrin, DDT, malathion, bendiocarb, and PBO synergist) and biochemical enzyme assays (P450, esterases, GST) for an Anopheles funestus population collected in Gbanikola, Bangui, Central African Republic in October 2014. No target-site mutation genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report target insecticide resistance markers.
Does not report extractable genotype data.
